<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="מנחם אב_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919688_theRebbe_695" batchId="meluket-_D7_9E_D7_A0_D7_97_D7_9D_20_D7_90_D7_91_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919688_theRebbe_695__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the interpretation placing "and her captives in charity" above "Zion will be redeemed through justice" aligns with the explanation in Likkutei Torah, where justice redeems Zion from the grasp of external forces, but charity is needed to return her to her original place.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">3)</t>
    <t s="2">And behold, this interpretation—that the aspect of "and her captives in charity" is higher than the aspect of "Zion will be redeemed through justice"—aligns with the explanation in Likkutei Torah and in the book of Likkutim of the Arizal13.</t>
    <t s="3">On the verse "Zion will be redeemed through justice,"</t>
    <t s="4">[except that there he explains the two aspects on a lower level],</t>
    <t s="5">for Zion is the point of Zion, the Yesod of Nukva, and because it is hollow and the lights are revealed there, that is where the external forces have a hold; therefore it says that through justice etc., they cause it to be redeemed and drive out the external forces from there.</t>
    <t s="6">But all this is only so that they should not take hold of her alone, and she will be recognizable there in her place, but she has not yet ascended to her first place and emerged from among them completely.</t>
    <t s="7">But in order to remove her from among them and to elevate her and seat her in her first place, one must perform etc. charity etc., and this is "and her captives in charity"—to return her to her place requires charity, and through the merit of charity she will return to her first place.</t>
    <t s="8">Thus, "and her captives in charity" is higher than "Zion will be redeemed through justice."</t>
    <t s="9">And this is also understood simply,</t>
    <t s="10">as it is written there,</t>
    <t s="11">that justice</t>
    <t s="12">(although justice is mercy14)</t>
    <t s="13">its essence is according to the strict line of law,</t>
    <t s="14">unlike charity, which is beyond the line of law.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses how the two interpretations of the verse are connected like a reversible seal, relating to the future superiority of action over study, as exemplified by the difference between the Mishkan (made of vegetation) and the Beis HaMikdash (made of stone), and the elevation of Yehudah (the inanimate) above Yosef (the vegetative).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">4)</t>
    <t s="2">And behold, it is explained elsewhere15</t>
    <t s="3">that interpretations that are on a single verse are related to each other,</t>
    <t s="4">and from this it is understood</t>
    <t s="5">that the interpretation that "and her captives in charity" is lower than "Zion will be redeemed through justice" has a connection with the interpretation that "and her captives in charity" is higher than "Zion will be redeemed through justice"</t>
    <t s="6">(and it is in the manner of the known concept16</t>
    <t s="7">regarding the matter of a reversible seal).</t>
    <t s="8">And the explanation is as follows:</t>
    <t s="9">It is known17</t>
    <t s="10">that our Sages, of blessed memory, said18</t>
    <t s="11">"Study is great now,</t>
    <t s="12">but in the days of Moshiach, action will be great."</t>
    <t s="13">And behold, study and action are analogous to the vegetative and the inanimate,</t>
    <t s="14">and in the future, action will be great,</t>
    <t s="15">for then the superiority of the inanimate will be revealed.</t>
    <t s="16">And it is in the manner explained elsewhere19</t>
    <t s="17">on the verse "And Yehudah approached him," regarding the difference between the Mishkan and the Beis HaMikdash</t>
    <t s="18">[that this matter has a special connection to Shabbos Chazon,</t>
    <t s="19">and as the Rader of Paritch wrote20</t>
    <t s="20">: And the depth of this matter will be explained</t>
    <t s="21">(that on Shabbos Chazon, the future Beis HaMikdash is shown to each person)</t>
    <t s="22">with what is explained elsewhere regarding the matter of "And Yehudah approached him,"</t>
    <t s="23">the history of our Temple etc.].</t>
    <t s="24">That the Mishkan was made of shittim wood,</t>
    <t s="25">cedars,</t>
    <t s="26">vegetation,</t>
    <t s="27">unlike the Beis HaMikdash, which was specifically made of stones and earth</t>
    <t s="28">(and it is forbidden to make protruding wood in it etc., as it is written21</t>
    <t s="29">"You shall not plant for yourself an asherah, any tree").</t>
    <t s="30">Because in the Beis HaMikdash there was a revelation of the superiority of the inanimate.</t>
    <t s="31">And the main revelation of the superiority of the inanimate will be in the future</t>
    <t s="32">(in the third Beis HaMikdash),</t>
    <t s="33">for then Yehudah will be elevated</t>
    <t s="34">(the aspect of the inanimate)</t>
    <t s="35">to be above Yosef</t>
    <t s="36">(the aspect of the vegetative),</t>
    <t s="37">as it is written22</t>
    <t s="38">"Behold, I will take the stick of Yosef etc. and place them upon it, the stick of Yehudah etc., and My servant Dovid shall be king over them etc., and Dovid My servant shall be their prince forever."23</t>
    <t s="39">For this is also what will be in the future—"action will be great,"</t>
    <t s="40">for the essence of Dovid is action,24</t>
    <t s="41">and as explained elsewhere25</t>
    <t s="42">regarding the difference between Dovid and Yehonason</t>
    <t s="43">(Malchus and Yesod, analogous to Yehudah and Yosef)</t>
    <t s="44">the son of Shaul,</t>
    <t s="45">that Yehonason the son of Shaul is the matter of study</t>
    <t s="46">(his service was according to Torah knowledge, unlike "to obey is better than sacrifice"</t>
    <t s="47">(the aspect of Kabbalas Ol of Dovid)</t>
    <t s="48">and it is said "Shaul from Rechovos HaNahar,"</t>
    <t s="49">for "Rechovos HaNahar" is the matter of understanding and comprehension,</t>
    <t s="50">study)</t>
    <t s="51">and Dovid is the aspect of action.</t>
    <t s="52">And it is said, "Until Dovid, he magnified."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that even now, when study is generally greater, there are matters where action is superior, and the emphasis on action in our times is because all future revelations depend on our actions during exile, as explained in Igeres HaKodesh regarding the primacy of charity in the era of Moshiach's footsteps.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">6)</t>
    <t s="2">And behold, although now study is great,</t>
    <t s="3">nevertheless there are several matters</t>
    <t s="4">(even now)</t>
    <t s="5">in which action is superior to study.</t>
    <t s="6">For example, that one suspends Torah study for a mitzvah that cannot be performed by others.26</t>
    <t s="7">And the content of Igeres HaKodesh, beginning "Hu v'Chayohi"</t>
    <t s="8">[which was written by the Alter Rebbe in the village of Poyena in the days before his passing27]</t>
    <t s="9">is about the superiority of practical mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="10">And the reason that even now they emphasize the superiority of action can be said to be because all the revelations of the future depend on our actions and service throughout the entire time of exile,28</t>
    <t s="11">and since in the future action will be great,</t>
    <t s="12">therefore even now they emphasize the superiority of action,</t>
    <t s="13">for through this the revelation of the future will come, when action will be great.</t>
    <t s="14">And in the manner explained in Igeres HaKodesh29</t>
    <t s="15">that our Sages, of blessed memory, did not say "Torah study is equivalent to acts of kindness" except in their days, but in these times, at the heels of Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="16">the primary service of G-d is the service of charity.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
